title: Magic Scarf: What Can It Be?
students: Draw 4 things a plain scarf could become in a pretend story, like a cape or a river, then circle one to act out.

title: One Stick, Many Stories
students: Match: draw a line from a stick used 4 ways (horse, wand, oar, fishing pole) to the pretend place where each is used.

title: Animal Actors: How Do They Move?
students: Trace 6 animal names under pictures, then circle how each one moves (hop, slither, stomp) before acting them out with the class.

title: Big Body, Small Body
students: Circle whether the actor makes a big or small body for 6 story characters: giant, mouse, tree, seed, bear and bug.

title: Goldilocks Story Order: Cut and Glue
students: Cut out 4 pictures from Goldilocks and the Three Bears and glue them in order: the walk, the porridge, the chairs, the beds.

title: The Wolf's Walk: Three Little Pigs Path
students: Draw the path the wolf walks from the straw house to the stick house to the brick house, then mark where each pig stands.

title: Sound Effect Story: The Rainy Day
students: Listen to a rain story read aloud and, at each of 5 stars, circle the body sound to make: tap, pat, clap or stomp.

title: Where Are We? Pretend Places
students: Draw yourself in 3 pretend places (a beach, a forest, outer space) and circle one thing your body would do in each.

title: Whose Hat Is It? Costume Match
students: Cut out 5 hats and glue each one on the character who would wear it in a play: chef, firefighter, king, wizard, farmer.

title: Freeze! Statue Poses
students: Draw a stick figure frozen statue for 3 feeling words read aloud (happy, scared, tired), then show the class one pose.

title: Our Pretend Story Plan
students: With a partner, draw who is in your pretend story, where it happens and one problem, in 3 picture boxes.

title: Stone Soup Pot: What Goes In Next?
students: Listen to Stone Soup, then glue 5 picture foods into the pot in the order the villagers bring them, ready to act out.

title: Jungle Path Maze: Right Moves Lead Out
students: Maze: at each of 5 forks, take the path whose move fits the animal pictured (frog hops, snake slithers), then act out all 5 moves.

title: I Can Pretend: Star Check
students: Fill in a star for each pretend skill shown in pictures (big body, small body, sounds, voice) and draw your favorite pretend role.

title: Pretend and Play Picture Review
students: Circle the right picture for 6 read-aloud questions about using body, voice, props and pretend places in a story.

title: Feelings Faces: Draw the Mouth
students: Draw the mouth and eyebrows on 4 blank puppet faces to show happy, sad, mad and surprised.

title: How Does the Puppet Feel?
students: Look at 6 puppet pictures with tilted heads or droopy arms and circle the feeling face that matches each one.

title: Paper Bag Puppet Plan
students: Draw the face for a paper bag puppet, circle the feeling it starts with, and circle its voice: high, low or squeaky.

title: Snail or Rabbit? Puppet Voice Speed
students: Listen to the teacher's puppet say one line 2 ways; circle the snail for slow or the rabbit for fast, then the feeling it shows.

title: What Does Fox Like?
students: After the teacher's fox puppet show, draw 3 things the fox likes and 1 thing it does not like.

title: The Lost Mitten Puppet Show Order
students: Cut and glue 4 scenes from a class puppet show about a lost mitten in the right order.

title: Before and After Faces
students: Draw the puppet's face before and after something happens (dropped ice cream, found a friend) for 3 short read-aloud stories.

title: Act It, Draw It: Feeling Words
students: For 4 feeling words read aloud (proud, shy, grumpy, excited), draw a puppet face and circle a body move that shows it.

title: Which Ending Do You Like?
students: Look at 2 picture endings to the puppet show, circle the one you like, and draw one reason why.

title: Bunny Puppet Likes What I Like
students: Circle the things the bunny puppet likes that you like too, from 8 pictures (rain, books, slides, carrots and more).

title: Good Puppet Show Audience
students: Circle 4 pictures that show a good puppet show audience (watching, clapping, quiet hands) and cross out 2 that do not.

title: Puppet Helper: The Fallen Tower
students: A puppet is sad its block tower fell; draw 2 ways another puppet could help, then circle how it feels after.

title: Puppets and Feelings Picture Review
students: Match 5 puppet poses to feelings, draw one feeling face, and circle fast or slow voice for 2 lines read aloud.

title: Join the Moon Crew: Pick Your Prop
students: Before Moon Base Drama, draw lines from 5 crew jobs (gardener, doctor, driver, cook, map maker) to the prop that shows each job.

title: My Crew Badge
students: Draw your role badge for the class drama: your job picture, your tool, and one thing you will say in role.

title: In Role or Not?
students: Look at 6 pictures and circle the children who are in role (wearing a costume piece, using a prop); cross out the others.

title: Moon Facts Save the Greenhouse
students: Circle the 3 true moon facts read aloud (no air, no rain, long cold nights) that help the crew save the plants.

title: Ask the Commander
students: Trace the question starter "Can we" and draw what you would ask the commander to help the moon crew.

title: Worried Farmer: Help the Garden
students: The teacher plays a worried farmer; draw 3 things the class does in role to help seeds grow: water, sun, pulling weeds.

title: Drama Story Map: Problem and Fix
students: Draw the problem in the class drama in box 1 and how the crew fixed it in box 2.

title: Change One Line, Change the Story
students: Hear 2 endings where one character says something different, and circle the picture that shows what happens in each.

title: Fruit Stand in Role
students: At a teacher-in-role fruit stand, count the fruit in 4 baskets (1 to 10) and draw the basket you buy in role.

title: Weather Reporter in Role
students: Circle the weather picture for 4 days read aloud, then draw yourself as a weather reporter holding a prop.

title: How Did Our Drama Go?
students: Circle a face for 3 questions (Did I stay in role? Use my prop? Listen?) and draw a favorite drama moment.

title: Drama in Role Picture Review
students: Circle the in-role pictures, match 4 props to jobs, and draw the class drama's problem and fix.

title: Who, Where, What? Story Starter
students: Draw a character, a setting and a problem in a 3-part story starter, then act out a 1-minute pretend story from it.

title: The Tortoise and the Hare: Race Order
students: Cut and glue 5 scenes from The Tortoise and the Hare in order, then write the animal's name under each.

title: Three Frozen Pictures: The Lion and the Mouse
students: Draw stick-figure frozen pictures (tableaux) for the beginning, middle and end of The Lion and the Mouse.

title: Voice Dial: Loud, Soft, High, Low
students: For 6 characters (giant, mouse, baby, robot, owl, queen), circle loud or soft and high or low, then say each line.

title: Moving Like Characters
students: Match 6 characters to movement words (stomp, tiptoe, wobble, glide, march, creep) and draw an arrow showing each one's path.

title: One Box, Many Stories
students: Draw a cardboard box becoming 4 things (car, boat, cave, robot) and write one word for what a character does with it.

title: Make the Storm: Sound Plan
students: Plan sounds for 4 moments in a storm story by choosing a body sound (rub, tap, snap, stomp) for each picture box.

title: Little Red Hen Playing Space
students: Draw a playing space for The Little Red Hen with the farm, the mill and the kitchen, and number where each scene happens.

title: Say It Like the Character
students: Read 5 short lines with a partner and circle how to say each one: happy, angry, sleepy or surprised.

title: What Does the Character Want?
students: Draw what 4 fable characters want (the fox wants the grapes) and circle yes or no for whether they get it.

title: Pretend Problem Solvers
students: Look at 3 picture problems (stuck kite, lost puppy, rainy picnic) and draw how a pretend character solves one, ready to act out.

title: Ant and Grasshopper Act-Out Plan
students: With a group, plan a 3-scene act-out of The Ant and the Grasshopper: who plays each part, one prop and one sound.

title: Two Stars and a Wish
students: After a group shares, draw 2 stars for things the actors did well (loud voice, big body) and write 1 wish.

title: Body, Voice or Imagination? Word Sort
students: Sort 9 picture-word cards (stomp, whisper, pretend and more) into body, voice and imagination, then act out one from each group.

title: Pretend and Play Check
students: Answer 6 picture questions about character, setting, voice and body, then draw a tableau of a favorite fable moment.

title: Feelings Thermometer: A Little or a Lot
students: Draw a puppet face for a little happy, medium happy and very happy on a thermometer, then do the same for mad.

title: Puppet Body Clues
students: Look at 6 puppet pictures and circle the body clue that shows each feeling: drooping head, bouncing, shaking or hiding.

title: Stick Puppet With a Want
students: Design a stick puppet: draw it, name it, and write one thing it wants and one thing it does not like.

title: Two Puppets, One Swing
students: Fill 2 speech bubbles for puppets who both want the last swing, using "I feel ___ because ___."

title: Why Does the Puppet Feel That Way?
students: Draw the cause and the feeling for 3 puppet moments (lost balloon, new friend, broken toy) in cause-and-feeling boxes.

title: Same Line, Three Feelings
students: Listen to one puppet line said 3 ways and draw the puppet's face and arms for each version.

title: Puppet Show Ticket Stub
students: After a puppet show, draw your favorite part, circle 2 feelings the puppet showed, and tell a partner how you knew.

title: Which Ending Won? Picture Graph
students: Make a picture graph of which of 3 puppet show endings the class liked best, then circle the winner and count the votes.

title: Shy Turtle Puppet
students: Circle things the shy turtle puppet does that people also do when shy, then draw one way to help the turtle.

title: Puppet Feelings Riddles
students: Solve 5 read-aloud riddles ("My ears droop, my tail is down") by circling the feeling, then make up one riddle.

title: New Feeling Words for Puppets
students: Draw puppet faces for 4 new words (nervous, calm, proud, lonely) and use one in the frame "The puppet felt ___ when ___."

title: Plan a Two-Puppet Scene
students: With a partner, draw 2 puppets, their feelings at the start and the end, and the one thing that changes them.

title: Puppets and Feelings Check
students: Match feelings to body clues, finish a cause-and-feeling box, and draw a puppet whose feeling changes.

title: Community Helpers in Role
students: Match 6 community helpers to their props and draw the one you would play in the class drama.

title: Town Meeting: The Broken Bridge
students: In role as townspeople, draw 2 ideas to fix the broken bridge and circle the helpers the town needs.

title: Ask the Mayor in Role
students: Finish 3 question starters (Who, Why, How) to ask the teacher in role as the town mayor.

title: True or Not? Moon Base Facts
students: Before Moon Base Drama, mark 6 sentences about the moon with a check for true or an X for not true.

title: My Role Card
students: Fill a role card: draw your character, write its name and job, and one thing it knows that helps the group.

title: Pond Scientists in Role
students: As scientists in a teacher-in-role pond drama, circle 4 animals that live in a pond and draw one to report on.

title: What Happened in Our Drama?
students: Draw the drama's 4 parts in order: the problem, the meeting, the plan and the ending.

title: Rewind: What If Someone Said No?
students: Draw what happened in the drama, then draw what might happen if one character said "No" instead.

title: Prop Detective
students: Look at 6 props and use clues read aloud to figure out which drama role each prop belongs to.

title: Drama Snapshot: Who Helped How?
students: Draw the class drama's final scene and label 3 roles with what each one did to help.

title: In-Role Self-Check
students: Circle yes or not yet for 4 drama skills (stayed in role, listened, used a fact, used my prop) and draw one goal.

title: Drama in Role Check
students: Answer 6 picture questions about roles, props and asking questions in role, then draw how the class drama was solved.

title: Story Mountain: The Enormous Turnip
students: Fill a 3-part story mountain for The Enormous Turnip, then circle which part has the most excitement for an audience.

title: Bremen Town Musicians Character Cards
students: Draw the 4 animal musicians, label one body move and one sound for each, then practice their walks.

title: Onstage, Offstage, Audience
students: Label a simple stage picture with onstage, offstage, backstage and audience, then draw where an actor waits to enter.

title: Write the Talking: Robber Scene
students: Write 4 speech bubbles for the scene where the Bremen Town animals scare the robbers out of the house.

title: Tableau Trio: The Turnip Pops Out
students: Plan a 3-person frozen picture of the turnip finally popping out, drawing each actor at a high, middle or low level.

title: Voice Choices: Momotaro
students: For 5 lines from the folktale Momotaro, choose speed, volume and feeling from word banks and mark symbols above the words.

title: Pantomime Puzzle: What Am I Holding?
students: Read 6 pantomime clue cards (brushing teeth, flying a kite), draw the invisible object each actor uses, then invent one.

title: Sensory Setting Walk
students: Imagine walking into a bakery, a forest and a beach; write one thing you see, hear and smell in each to help you act it.

title: Mirror Game Log
students: Record 3 mirror game rounds: who led, the moves tried, and circle how closely the partners matched.

title: Want, Problem, Solution: Three Folktales
students: Fill a want-problem-solution chart for characters in 3 folktales: The Fisherman and His Wife, Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom, and Momotaro.

title: Turn a Story Into a Scene
students: Fill in the blank script: rewrite 4 sentences of The Little Red Hen as a short scene with character names, spoken lines and one action in parentheses.

title: Our Story Play Plan
students: Plan a 4-scene story play: list the characters, draw the setting, and choose 2 props and 1 sound effect.

title: Rehearsal Checklist Log
students: Track 3 rehearsals, checking loud voice, facing the audience and staying in character, and write one thing to fix each time.

title: Two Glows and a Grow
students: Watch a group's story play and write 2 things that worked, using words like voice or face, and 1 suggestion.

title: Pretend and Play Review
students: Label stage areas, fill a short story mountain, and rewrite 2 story sentences as lines of dialogue.

title: Shadow Puppet Design
students: Design a shadow puppet: draw its outline, mark where the stick attaches, and note its feeling at the start of the story.

title: Two Feelings at Once
students: Draw a puppet that feels excited and nervous at the same time on a first day, and label the body clue for each feeling.

title: The Lost Kite: Feelings Chart
students: Chart a puppet's feeling at the beginning, middle and end of a story about a lost kite, and what caused each change.

title: Same Spill, Two Puppets
students: Write how one event (spilled paint) feels to 2 different puppets, using "I felt ___ when ___ because ___."

title: Puppet Moves Color by Code
students: Color by code: read the puppet move in each numbered space (head tilt, quick bounce, turn away); the feeling it shows picks the color.

title: What Do the Puppets Like? Bar Graph
students: Read a chart of what 4 puppets like to eat and play, make a bar graph, and answer 3 questions about their preferences.

title: Puppet Show Review Card
students: Rate a puppet show on 3 criteria (clear feelings, clear voices, story) with stars and give a reason for each rating.

title: Kind Words for Puppets
students: Read 4 puppet problems (left out of a game, scared of thunder) and write one kind sentence a friend puppet could say to each.

title: Feeling Word Ladders
students: Order feeling words from mild to strong on 2 ladders (glad, happy, thrilled; annoyed, mad, furious) and pick a puppet move for each.

title: The Brave Mouse and Me
students: Fill a Venn diagram comparing the brave mouse puppet's likes with your own likes, then write one sentence about them.

title: Puppet Play Script Starter
students: Write a 6-line puppet script for 2 characters whose feelings change, with a stage direction box for each line.

title: Puppet Rehearsal Log
students: Track 3 puppet rehearsals: voice clear, puppet faces the audience, feelings show, plus one fix for next time.

title: Puppets and Feelings Review
students: Rank feeling words, read puppet body clues, and chart how one puppet's feelings change across a short story.

title: Expert Badge: Beehive in Trouble
students: Choose a role in a teacher-in-role drama about a beehive in trouble and write 3 facts your expert knows.

title: How Bees Help Plants
students: Read a short passage about bees and flowers, answer 4 questions, and underline facts to use in role.

title: Hot Seat Questions
students: Write 4 questions for the worried beekeeper in the hot seat, starting with who, what, why and how.

title: Letter to the Mayor in Role
students: In role as a town gardener, write a 4-sentence letter asking the mayor to plant more flowers for bees.

title: Lost Traveler Map
students: Use a simple town map in a teacher-in-role drama to guide a lost traveler, drawing the route and labeling 3 landmarks.

title: Props That Tell the Story
students: Draw 4 props for the drama and write what each one tells the audience about a character or the place.

title: Drama Decision Tree
students: Draw the choice the class made in the drama and 2 other paths it could have taken, with what would follow.

title: Thought Tracking: Frozen Moment
students: Draw 3 characters frozen at the drama's big moment and write a thought bubble showing what each one is thinking.

title: Moon Base Crew Report
students: After Moon Base Drama, fill a crew report with the problem, the true moon fact the crew used, and the solution.

title: Rewrite a Line, Change the Path
students: Rewrite one line from the class drama 2 different ways and explain how each choice changes what happens next.

title: Drama Self-Check
students: Rate yourself on 4 in-role skills, write one fact you used in role, and set one goal for the next drama.

title: Drama in Role Review
students: Answer questions about hot seating, thought tracking and teacher in role, then plan one question for a new drama.

title: Actor's Toolbox: Voice, Body, Imagination
students: Label an actor outline with the 3 actor tools and draw one way to use each tool for a fable character.

title: Volume, Pace and Pitch: The Fox and the Crow
students: Mark 6 lines from The Fox and the Crow with symbols for loud or soft, fast or slow, high or low, then perform them.

title: Character Walks
students: For 5 characters (a king, a sneaky cat, a tired farmer, a robot, a toddler), circle speed, weight and level, then sketch one walk.

title: Parts of a Script
students: Label a short script page: title, character list, character names, dialogue and stage directions in parentheses.

title: Script Words Crossword
students: Solve a crossword with 10 real clues about scripts (dialogue, stage direction, cast, cue, role), then use 2 of the words in sentences.

title: Town Mouse, Country Mouse Traits
students: Read a 10-line scene from The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse and list 2 traits for each mouse with a line as evidence.

title: Inside and Outside Character Map
students: Fill a character map for the crow: how it looks, moves and sounds, and what it wants.

title: Stage Directions Fix-Up
students: Add stage directions to 6 lines of a script so the actor knows how to move or feel (crosses to the door, whispering).

title: Readers Theater: The Lion and the Mouse
students: Read a 4-part readers theater script, highlight one part, mark voice choices, and answer 3 questions about the characters.

title: Write a Two-Character Scene
students: Write an 8-line scene for 2 characters about a lost library book, with a problem and stage directions.

title: Getting Off Book: Rehearsal Plan
students: Plan 4 rehearsals for a short scene: what to practice each day, who helps, and a check box for memorized lines.

title: Voice and Body Rehearsal Log
students: Log 4 rehearsals: lines known, one voice choice tried, one body choice tried, and what changed.

title: Character Choices Self-Check
students: Rate how clearly your voice, body and face showed your character and write one choice to make stronger.

title: Characters and Scenes Review
students: Label a script page, match voice choices to characters, and add stage directions to 4 lines.

title: Community Issue or One-Time Problem?
students: Sort 8 situations into community issues and one-time problems, then circle the issue your group could turn into a play.

title: Neighbors Who Want Things
students: Create 3 characters affected by a littered park (a park worker, a dog walker, a kid) and write what each one wants.

title: Park Cleanup Play Story Map
students: Map a short play about the littered park: setting, characters, problem, 3 events and solution.

title: Interview a Neighbor Character
students: Write 4 interview questions and in-character answers for a made-up neighbor who cares about the park.

title: Three-Scene Plan
students: Plan the beginning, middle and end scenes of the park play: who is onstage, what happens and one line that shows the problem.

title: Toy Theater Set: The Park
students: Draw a paper toy theater set for the park scene with a backdrop, 2 set pieces and arrows where actors enter.

title: One-Piece Costume Sheet
students: Design one costume piece for each character and explain how it shows that character's job or personality.

title: Write the Big Decision Scene
students: Write an 8-line scene where the characters agree on a plan to fix the park, with stage directions.

title: Crew Jobs Chart
students: Assign group jobs (actors, prop maker, sound person, stage manager) and write each job's tasks and a finish date.

title: Fix-It List: Rehearsal Notes
students: During 3 rehearsals, list what worked and what to fix in each scene, then check off fixes as they happen.

title: Come to Our Play: Poster
students: Design a paper poster for the community play with title, issue, time and one line that hooks the audience.

title: Did Our Message Land?
students: Answer 4 questions about the play's message, how the audience reacted, and one change for next time.

title: Plays About Our Community Review
students: Sort issue examples, finish a story map for a new issue, and match production jobs to their tasks.

title: Good Audience Checklist
students: Circle 6 good audience behaviors in a picture of a theater and explain 2 of them in a sentence.

title: I Noticed, I Wondered
students: While watching a short scene, write 3 things noticed (voice, movement, costume) and 2 questions.

title: Two Versions of The Fox and the Grapes
students: Compare a slow, sad version and a fast, silly version of one scene on a T-chart of voice, movement and mood.

title: What Made the Difference?
students: After the Audience Talkback tool, list what changed between 2 versions (costume, lights, voice, music) and circle the change that mattered most.

title: What Makes a Scene Work? Criteria Picker
students: Choose 3 criteria from a list (clear voice, believable character, good pace) and write what each looks like onstage.

title: Star Ratings With Reasons
students: Rate 2 versions of a scene on 3 criteria with stars, then write a reason for each rating using "because."

title: My Favorite Version Paragraph
students: Write an opinion paragraph naming the version you prefer, with 2 reasons from the scene and a closing sentence.

title: Feedback Sandwich
students: Turn 4 blunt comments ("It was bad") into helpful feedback with a compliment, a suggestion and another compliment.

title: Mood Line for a Scene
students: Mark a scene's mood at 5 moments on a line graph from calm to tense and explain the highest point.

title: Feelings Evidence in a Script
students: Read a short original scene and answer 4 questions, including two "find the line that shows" items about a character's feelings.

title: Actor Choice or Design Choice?
students: Sort 10 response words (expression, gesture, pace, costume, lighting) into actor choices and design choices and use 3 in sentences.

title: My Audience Goals
students: Rate yourself as an audience member and responder and set 2 goals for the next show you watch.

title: Responding to Plays Review
students: Compare 2 short scene descriptions with criteria, rewrite a comment as helpful feedback, and give a star rating with a reason.

title: I Want, But: Objectives and Obstacles
students: For 6 short scene situations, fill in the blanks "I want to ___ but ___" to name each character's objective and obstacle.

title: Tactics Toolbox: Borrow the Bike
students: Brainstorm 5 tactics (beg, bargain, trick, charm, demand) a character could use to borrow a bike, then star the strongest and explain why.

title: The Emperor's New Clothes: Cast Cards
students: Read a short original retelling of The Emperor's New Clothes and fill 4 cast cards with each character's want, fear and voice.

title: Stage Areas Grid Game
students: Draw and label the 9 stage areas on a grid, then follow 6 blocking directions with a paper game piece and mark where it ends.

title: Blocking Shorthand Decoder
students: Decode 8 blocking notes written in shorthand (X DSL, ENT UR) into plain words, then write 2 of your own for a partner.

title: Secret Backstory File
students: Fill a "classified" file for one of the trickster weavers: hometown, what they want, a secret, and a line only they would say.

title: Conflict Match-Up
students: Match 6 short scene summaries to conflict types (character vs. character, self, nature or society) and justify one match in a sentence.

title: Fix the Script Format
students: Find and fix 8 formatting mistakes (missing names, stage directions out of parentheses) in a messy script page.

title: Parade Scene Adaptation
students: Adapt the parade moment from The Emperor's New Clothes into a 10-line scene for 3 characters with stage directions.

title: Character Body Blueprint
students: Draw and label a character outline with posture, gesture, walk and one habit, explaining how each shows personality.

title: Five-Day Vocal Warm-Up Log
students: Log 5 days of warm-ups (breathing, tongue twisters, projection) and rate clarity and volume each day on a 1 to 4 scale.

title: Scene Partner Rehearsal Plan
students: Plan a partner rehearsal: 2 goals, beats to run, blocking to set, and a line-check box for each partner.

title: Scene Showcase Rubric
students: Score your scene on objective, voice, body and blocking with a 4-level rubric and write 2 sentences on what to improve.

title: Characters and Scenes Task Cards
students: Work through 10 cut-apart task-card strips: name objectives, label stage areas, fix script format and choose tactics.

title: Neighborhood Survey Bar Graph
students: Graph an invented survey of 50 residents about 4 neighborhood issues, then pick the issue a play should tackle and explain.

title: The Missing Crosswalk: Four Viewpoints
students: Fill a viewpoint chart for a crossing guard, a driver, a student and a shop owner about a busy street with no crosswalk.

title: Welcome Wagon: A New Family Arrives
students: Brainstorm how 4 invented neighbor characters might welcome or misunderstand a new family moving in, and what each wants.

title: One-Sentence Play Pitch
students: Write a logline for a community play using the frame "When ___, a ___ must ___ before ___." and test it on a partner.

title: Scene Breakdown Strips
students: Fill 4 scene strips for a crosswalk play with setting, characters, conflict and the line that ends each scene, then order them.

title: Toy Theater Build Sheet
students: Design a paper toy theater: draw the backdrop, 3 set pieces and paper character cutouts, labeling materials for each.

title: Costume Design Plate: Show Who They Are
students: Draw and label costumes for 3 characters with colors and fabrics, and explain what each choice tells the audience.

title: Prop Hunt List
students: List every prop the play needs, who brings or makes it, and which scene uses it, then check for any missing props.

title: Town Hall Scene
students: Write a 12-line town hall scene where characters with different views about the crosswalk argue and reach a decision.

title: Production Timeline: Idea to Opening
students: Cut and order 10 production steps (choose issue, write, cast, rehearse, tech, perform) on a timeline with invented dates.

title: Rehearsal Progress Log
students: Track 4 rehearsals: scenes run, problems found, fixes tested, and who needs extra practice.

title: Playbill Design
students: Design a fold-over playbill for the class play with cast list, crew jobs, a scene list and a short note about the issue.

title: Plays About Our Community Review
students: Read a short community scenario and plan a mini play: characters, viewpoints, 3 scenes and one design choice.

title: Watching With Criteria
students: Before watching, choose 4 criteria and write what strong work looks like for each, then take notes under each while watching.

title: Two Emperors: Funny vs. Serious
students: Compare 2 versions of the parade scene (funny and serious) on voice, movement, costume and how the crowd reacts.

title: Design Changes the Feeling
students: Note how lights, music and costume differed in 2 versions of a scene and how each change shifted your feelings.

title: Evidence or Just Opinion? Cut and Sort
students: Cut and sort 10 audience comments into opinion with evidence or opinion without evidence, then fix 3 weak ones.

title: Claim, Evidence, Reason
students: Write a claim about a scene, give 2 pieces of evidence from the performance, and explain why each matters.

title: Script vs. Stage
students: Read a short script excerpt and a description of how it was staged, then answer 4 questions about what changed and why.

title: Laugh and Gasp Tally
students: Tally laughs, gasps and silences during 2 versions of a scene, graph them side by side, and explain what caused the difference.

title: Actor Spotlight
students: Pick one actor in a scene and evaluate 3 choices (voice, gesture, timing) with evidence and one suggestion.

title: Response Words Cloze
students: Complete a cloze passage, a short review of a scene, using 8 words (criteria, pacing, mood, interpretation, blocking, justify).

title: I Noticed, I Wonder, What If
students: Practice 3 rounds of peer feedback on classmate scenes using the starters "I noticed," "I wonder" and "What if."

title: Tale to Today Connection
students: Connect a choice the Emperor makes to a book or event you know, explaining in 4 sentences how the two are alike.
